Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Allie Carl/Axios
 

Emptying out the notebook as we head into the weekend...

🎓 Academia: Harvard University yesterday released its annual financial report, and it was the mixed bag one might imagine.

  • Plus side: The world's largest endowment generated a 27.1% return, easily besting the S&P 500 and rising to nearly $68 billion. Venture capital played a key role, perhaps validating a Yale Model that had been falling out of favor.
  • Minus side: Most endowment monies are restricted — i.e., can't be used for general purposes — and Harvard has been under relentless attack by the Trump administration (research grant freezes, international student bans, large endowment tax, etc.). In fact, a spokesperson tells me that ongoing and one-time legal fees totaled around $210 million during the fiscal year. To make budgets work, the university has had to do layoffs and keep some other roles unfilled.
  • Irony side: One of the people responsible for helping Harvard keep its financial equilibrium might be Trump pal Elon Musk, as the school recently disclosed a multibillion-dollar investment in SpaceX.

🗓️ IPO calendar: Anthropic still appears to be on track to go public in 2026, having just shared Q3 financials with prospective investors, but time is a'ticking.

  • Let's assume that it wants to price before Thanksgiving week and that it plans to match SpaceX's lightning-fast speed (16 biz days between the S-1 flip and listing).
  • That gives Anthropic a flip deadline of Oct. 29 or 30, depending on how you view Veterans Day. But next week feels more likely, to build in a bit of cushion.
  • In the meantime, what do we think the ticker symbol will be? I've seen a bunch of "DOOM" suggestions on social media, but an even more flippant one might be "SAMA."

💊 Magic wand: AI drug developer Iambic Therapeutics closed its first day of trading up more than 18%, and I spoke briefly with CEO Tom Miller.

  • He emphasized that the company's lead oncology drug has been administered to more than 100 patients, rather than just being simulated in models, and said he views the VC valuation for Isomorphic as validation for Iambic's growth story.
  • I also asked him about the recent claim that some AI researchers have taken up smoking to signal their faith in the technology's ability to cure cancer. Miller looked a bit shocked, and then replied: "I think it's important to not regard AI as a magic wand. And Iambic has never pitched ourselves as an AI magic wand."

❓ Quiz time: Can you name the family office manager who just spun out and raised an independent fund? Hint: The family in question has more than one family office.

🎲 Where in the world: Flying out to Vegas on Sunday for a brief stop at Money 2020. Hope to see some of you there...

 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images
 

Proofpoint, backed by Thoma Bravo, agreed to buy Miami-based data security firm Varonis Systems (Nasdaq: VRNS) for $6.3 billion in cash.

Why it's the BFD: This is the largest cybersecurity deal announced in 2026.

  • It also may make Proofpoint more attractive to the public markets. The company originally hoped to IPO this year, but so far hasn't filed.

By the numbers: Varonis shareholders would receive $49.75 per share. That's a 52% premium to the closing price before the first reports in June of a possible sale, but still a discount to where Varonis traded one year ago.

The bottom line: "Proofpoint positions itself as a human and agent-based threat protection layer, but it really doesn't have data security like data classification and permissions tracking. Varonis brings that, making Proofpoint's AI story more believable." — Chris Metinko, Axios Pro
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

🚑 Estuary Biotherapeutics, a developer of gene therapies for kidney disease, raised $103m in seed and Series A funding from RA Capital Management, 4BIO Capital, GV, Deep Track Capital, Biogen New Ventures, and UPMC Enterprises. axios.link/4dCPGd8

• Stand, an SF-based startup that insures homes in catastrophe-exposed regions, raised $70m in Series C funding at a $1b valuation. Saga Ventures led, joined by Lowercarbon, Eclipse, Equal Ventures, Inspired Capital, Neotribe, and Jackson Square Ventures. axios.link/4yY1VJU

• Mueon, a Portland, Ore.-based semiconductor systems startup, raised $65m in Series A funding. Maverick Silicon led, joined by Intel Capital, IQT, M-Ventures, and Oregon Venture Fund. axios.link/4Ba8xWV

⚡️ Rabot Energy, a German platform for turning homes into virtual power plants, raised $50m in Series B funding. Endeit led, joined by DTCF and insiders HV Capital, HTGF, Bosch Ventures, CNI, Acurio Ventures and Vent.io. axios.link/4joRz0K

⚡️ Holyvolt, a Swedish AI battery materials discovery startup, raised $45m from Fifth Wall, Zone II, and CC VC. axios.link/4dHduMP

🚑 Seragy, a German biomarker startup, raised €12m from Commerzbank, the MB, and the State of Lower Saxony. axios.link/4dEnPJr

• Fission, a NYC-based provider of liquidity infrastructure for tokenized investment funds, raised $10m in Series A funding. Pantera Capital led, joined by Circle Ventures, Borderless Capital, Ari Rubenstein, New Form, gumi Cryptos Capital, Anthony Scaramucci, Manhattan Venture Partners, Reflexive Capital, and Lattice Capital. axios.link/4ioUc1i

• Solvera, an Oslo-based AI construction engineering firm, raised $6.3m in pre-seed funding. Seedcamp led, joined by Construct Venture, Inception Fund, Momentum, Obos Ventures, PSV Tech, Sondo, and The Nordic Web Ventures. axios.link/4Be09py

• Shamrock AI, an India-based data testing platform for agentic AI, raised $5m in seed funding. Endiya Partners led, joined by Capria Ventures. axios.link/4B83HcN
 
 

A MESSAGE FROM J.P. MORGAN

A banking team for the AI era
 
 

Sid Sheth, co-founder of tech company d-Matrix, knew he needed a banking team that could keep up with the demands of the rapidly evolving AI landscape. J.P. Morgan was the right choice because of its speed and scale, which helped the company expand internationally.

Private Equity Deals
 

• 26North Partners agreed to acquire MEI Industrial Solutions, a Coppell, Texas-based provider of equipment execution services, from Olympus Partners. axios.link/4yUxl3K

• Apax Partners agreed to buy out Warburg Pincus' stake in Dutch telco Odido. axios.link/4hQmC4l

• Atlas Holdings and Lone Star Funds are weighing bids for International Paper's (NYSE: IP) European packaging business (fka DS Smith), which has been expected to go public, per the FT. axios.link/4s8ZwJx

• First Class Air, backed by O2 Investment Partners, invested in Vertical Aerospace, a Bristow, Okla.-based aircraft MRO. axios.link/3VQvcaC

• GHK Capital Partners acquired USA Hometown Experts, a residential services platform in the Southeastern U.S. axios.link/4ySe8Qg

⚡️Integrated Power Services, backed by Searchlight Capital Partners, acquired Bold Renewables, a Windsor, Colo.-based maintenance and parts provider for solar inverters. axios.link/4yp88gC

• Mubadala Capital completed its $6.2b take-private buyout of Clear Channel Outdoor. axios.link/4jZMgEZ

• PACT Capital Partners acquired a passive minority stake in midmarket PE firm Sterling Investment Partners. axios.link/4ynhWrA

• Transaction Network Services, backed by Koch Equity Development, acquired Netnumber, a Marlborough, Mass.-based provider of phone number intelligence and registry services, from Abry Partners. axios.link/47ikdcD
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

• Great Hill Partners hired Jefferies to find a buyer for Custom Ink, a custom-designed apparel maker that could fetch nearly $1.5b, per Reuters. axios.link/3WtHQwo

• Intuit (Nasdaq: INTU) agreed to acquire Sequence, a U.K. revenue and payroll management platform, for around $200m. Sequence backers include 645 Ventures, a16z, Firstminute Capital, Passion Capital, DIG Ventures, Mischief, and Vor Capital. axios.link/4yp8kN6
 
 
More M&A
 

• Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) agreed to sell its Fiberon composite decking business to Inteplast Group. axios.link/4dIzFlS

• Irenic Capital became the second activist investor to push for U.K. self-storage group Big Yellow (LSE: BYG) to consider a sale, per the FT. axios.link/4jjsrZ9

• International Seaways (NYSE: INSW) agreed to acquire Bruton (Oslo: BRUT), including four VLCC vessels, for around $370m. axios.link/4s69ZWl

🚑 Labcorp (NYSE: LH) agreed to buy the lab testing business of BioReference Health from OPKO Health (Nasdaq: OPK) for $722m in cash upfront and $150m of potential earnouts. axios.link/3UvqM8L

⚡️Sakuu, a San Jose, Calif.-based battery machine manufacturer, plans to go public at an implied $600m valuation via a reverse merger with Pyrophyte Acquisition Corp. II (NYSE: PAII). Sakuu previously tried a deSPAC in 2023 and has raised VC funding from firms like MissionBlue Capital Partners, CSVE Ventures and Musashi Seimitsu Industry Co. axios.link/4euUGR9
 
 
Fundraising
 

• Aldaron, a new PE firm focused on using AI to increase portfolio company revenue, raised $885m for its debut fund. axios.link/4ytgiVb

🚑 Catalio Capital Management is raising $500m for its fifth "Nexus" fund, per Bloomberg. axios.link/47j49r0

• EMK raised €1.25b for a single-asset CV focused on VDK Group, a European provider of tech installation services. axios.link/47rzNCH
 
 
It's Personnel
 

Partners Group laid off or reassigned "dozens" of employees in its 200-person private equity unit, per Bloomberg.

• Bow River Capital promoted Greg Hiatrides to CEO. He previously led PE for Bow River and succeeds Blair Richardson, who transitions to chairman. axios.link/3VN9FzC

• Harmonic Growth Partners promoted Daniel Vernic to partner. axios.link/3VJftdu

🌎 Lucie Hankin joined climate-focused VC firm Overture as a partner. She previously was with True Vectors. axios.link/4dHPYPN

• Rich Peacock is joining JPMorgan as global head of consumer and retail M&A, per Reuters. He previously was with Bank of America. axios.link/4imNjh8
